purpose: Declare which social platforms this network posts to (see platforms, which is the switch), how a paused platform behaves (see pause_mode), and prevent long-term starvation of smaller brands on the enabled ones while preserving daily caps.

platforms._read_me_first: This block is the on/off switch for each social platform. Nothing else in the repository decides whether a platform posts. To turn one on or off, change its "enabled" value here and commit. That is the entire change. A platform switched OFF must also record who paused it, when and why, plus a "pause_mode" saying what happens to its content meanwhile: "dormant" means nothing is produced at all (LinkedIn), and "delivery_route" means the platform's own API lane is off while a declared delivery route carries the same posts (X, through Buffer). Neither mode ever asks a human to post anything -- a post the route has no room for stays queued and goes out on a later run. pause_mode is ignored while enabled is true, so re-enabling a platform stays a one-boolean change either way.

x.HOW_TO_TURN_X_BACK_ON: Change "enabled" on the next line from false to true, and commit. That is the whole switch, exactly as it is for LinkedIn. The X entries already sitting in data/social-queue.json start going out again on their own -- they were never deleted, never re-labelled and carry no per-row pause mark, so nothing has to be rebuilt or un-marked. "pause_mode" below is inert the moment enabled is true; leave it as it is. X's API is pay-per-use and a post carrying a URL costs about $0.20, so turning this on means funding the developer account first -- until then every write answers HTTP 402 credits-depleted. While it is off, distribution does NOT stop: Buffer carries it, for nothing. See delivery_route below.
x.paused_reason: owner_decision_2026-08-29: "im not funding X so find a $0 workaround or kill it." X's API is pay-per-use with no free tier -- every write this repository has ever made answered HTTP 402 problems/credits-depleted, starting with the very first request, and nothing has ever posted. At roughly $0.20 per post with a URL, eight a day is about $48/month. The owner has decided not to pay it. This is NOT a dormant pause: X is off for API POSTING only, and distribution continues through the delivery route below. That is what pause_mode "delivery_route" means and why it is not "dormant" like LinkedIn. It used to mean a sheet the owner worked through herself; that was retired on 2026-08-29 when she said "this means i manually have to do it? i will never do it honestly", and Buffer replaced it entirely. Nothing in this repository asks her to do anything now.

delivery_route._read_me_first: A delivery route is another way for an X post to LEAVE, and since 2026-08-29 it is the ONLY way: it is not a second platform and it does not change what is posted -- the same queue, the same priority order, the same brand rotation, the same text. X's own API stays off and is contacted zero times; it is pay-per-use at about $0.20 per post carrying a URL, and every post here carries one. Buffer publishes to the same X profile from its free plan at no per-post cost. Turn it off by setting "enabled" below to false: X then distributes nothing and its entries simply wait in the queue. There is no fallback lane and nothing asks the owner to do anything -- the sheet she was once expected to work through was retired the day Buffer started carrying the posts.
delivery_route.credential: BUFFER_ACCESS_TOKEN (repository secret; never in this file)
delivery_route.channel: Discovered at runtime, and ONLY a channel whose Buffer service is "twitter" (Buffer's schema has no "x" service). Never "the first channel": this Buffer account also carries iamcindymercer, a TikTok channel belonging to a different project of the owner's, and scripts/lib/buffer_route.py re-checks the selected channel's service before posting and again before every post so that channel can never be chosen. Not pinned here, so reconnecting the X profile in Buffer does not require a commit.
delivery_route.queued_is_not_published: Buffer ACCEPTING a post is not X publishing it. An accepted entry is stamped status "buffer_queued" with its Buffer post id, and Buffer sends it at the channel's next posting slot. Nothing in this repository reports it as posted.
delivery_route.STATUS_2026_08_29: Live. The X channel sequoia_ta12767 (service "twitter") is connected and Buffer accepts posts for it. The retired hand-post sheet is gone: what Buffer's free plan has no room for stays queued_for_auto_post and goes out on a later run, counted in reports/social-publisher-report.json under deferred_waiting_for_delivery_route.
delivery_route.limits: Discovered at runtime on EVERY run, never hardcoded, and the strictest one binds. Three different kinds apply at once and all three are read from Buffer's own API: (1) the channel's daily RATE from dailyPostingLimits -- 50 for this X channel; (2) the free plan's standing QUEUE DEPTH from account.organizations.limits.scheduledPosts -- 10, meaning ten posts may sit waiting at once, which is far stricter than the rate and is what actually governs; and (3) daily_limit above, this network's own decision. Because the binding limit is a depth rather than a rate, the route TOPS THE QUEUE UP to just under it rather than pushing a fixed number per day, and adds more only as Buffer drains. A number typed here stays wrong after Buffer changes it or the plan changes, and being wrong about a ceiling is what produced 581 requests in 76 seconds on 2026-08-29.
delivery_route.costs_nothing: The owner pays Buffer nothing, which is the entire reason this route exists rather than X's paid API. Nothing here buys, trials or upgrades anything, and the route never posts past a refusal to see what happens: a limit or plan refusal halts it for the run, is recorded by name, and is not retried.

linkedin.HOW_TO_TURN_LINKEDIN_BACK_ON: Change "enabled" on the next line from false to true, and commit. That is the whole switch. The 581 LinkedIn posts already sitting in data/social-queue.json start going out again on their own -- they were never deleted, never re-labelled, and nothing has to be rebuilt or un-marked. Two repository secrets also have to exist for a post to actually send: LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN and LINKEDIN_AUTHOR_URN. If you flip this on before adding them, nothing breaks: each run says "linkedin_on_but_uncredentialled" in reports/social-publisher-report.json and nothing else changes. (X's own API is off too -- it is paused with pause_mode "delivery_route", so its content goes out through Buffer's free queue instead. Nothing about either platform asks a human to post anything.)
linkedin.paused_reason: owner_decision_2026-08-29: "drop linkedin for now its not important", and "i might bring linkedin back at anytime". LinkedIn is paused on purpose and is expected to come back. It is NOT off because LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN / LINKEDIN_AUTHOR_URN are missing from repository secrets -- that absence follows from this decision rather than causing it. This record exists so "paused by choice", "on but uncredentialled" and "on and posting" are three visibly different states instead of one blank secret.

rotation.rule: Sort by prior posted count divided by quota weight, then rotate the brand start position by date ordinal.
rotation.guarantee: No brand is permanently locked behind earlier queue order when eligible posts exist.

dream-wedding-builder.rule: Four domains do not create four separate social allocations.
